findings: readPacket sets _eof=true for any negative av_read_frame result, logging non-EOF via macro that does not increment _errorCount. decodeFrame then sends null packet to drain. Thus demux failure can take same termination route as normal EOF without direct errorCount increment; not full decoder runtime reproduction.

nextFrame returns bool for decodeFrameFiltered failure and conversion failure alike; no typed EOF-versus-error return. Separate errorCount counts some codec send/receive failures but does not establish complete enumeration of demux/convert failures.

Successful receive computes estimated frame number from best_effort_timestamp and stream rate; equal prior estimate increments by1, backwards iframe numbers warn. These are estimates, not explicit presentation timestamp ledger or variable-rate frame identity guarantee.

ptsToFrame/frameToPts use floating rational conversion and nominal r_frame_rate; no validation visible in these helper bodies for zero/missing rates. Open/seek implementation not fully read, so no claim that missing-rate inputs necessarily reach them.

Header documents fast seek inaccurate, accurate seek decodes from I-frame, close retains metadata, lastFrameNumber useful iframe-only. Full implementations remain partial; interface comments alone not runtime accuracy proof.

Metadata stores duration integerseconds and frameRate float, renders QTime-based strings; textual duration is not a full long-clip/rational timing oracle. Audio metadata presence does not imply audio duplicate confirmation.
